coverage: Premarket, Fri Nov 13 (data through the Thu Nov 12 close)
moodReason: Hot October inflation has traders fully pricing a December rate hike, the 10-year Treasury yield climbed back to about 5.1%, and oil rose after Trump said he is no longer interested in a deal with Iran. Stocks still gained 2.9% for the week, but the rate and oil backdrop leans negative.

stories.headline: October CPI comes in hotter than expected on headline and core prices
stories.what: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October against a 0.3% forecast, and core prices rose 0.3% against a 0.2% forecast. The BLS published no 12-month rate because October 2025 data was not collected during last year's government shutdown.
stories.why: CME FedWatch shows a quarter-point hike at the Dec 8 to 9 meeting fully priced, with about 13.6 percent odds of a half-point move. Higher expected rates raise borrowing costs and pressure equity valuations.

stories.headline: 10-year Treasury yield climbs back above 5% on Fed hike bets and higher oil
stories.what: After the Veterans Day holiday, bond markets reopened with the 10-year yield rising more than 13 basis points to about 5.12 percent intraday. The 2-year yield rose to about 4.88 percent. The Treasury's official par yield for the 10-year was 5.10 percent.
stories.why: A 5 percent 10-year yield raises the discount rate used to value stocks and raises mortgage and corporate borrowing costs, which weighs on the broad market.

stories.headline: Oil rises after Trump says he is no longer interested in an Iran deal
stories.what: Oil prices climbed on Thursday after President Trump said he is no longer interested in a deal with Iran. Reports also described U.S. forces downing two Iranian attack drones.
stories.why: Higher crude adds to inflation pressure, which strengthens the case for Fed hikes. Sources differ on the exact Brent level, with reported prices around 92 to 96 dollars a barrel.

stories.headline: Stocks recover from a sharp early drop but still close slightly lower
stories.what: The S&P 500 fell nearly 1 percent early on Thursday, erased the loss, then finished down 0.4 percent. The Russell 2000 underperformed with a 1.7 percent decline. For the week, the S&P 500 is up 2.9 percent and the Nasdaq up 3.2 percent.
stories.why: The quick recovery shows dip buyers are still active, but the small-cap underperformance suggests investors are sensitive to higher rates.

watch.item: Pre-market trading after a mixed Thursday close, with oil and Iran headlines in focus
FOMC meeting, where a quarter-point hike is fully priced and a half-point move has some odds

bottomLine: The S&P 500 still gained 2.9 percent this week, but the tone has turned cautious. Hot inflation has moved the Fed toward another hike, pushing the 10-year yield back near 5 percent, and oil is rising as Iran talks stall. Until inflation cools or the oil picture improves, rate expectations and energy prices are the main risks for stocks.
